title: Dynamic constrained dialogue for Freya: implementation decision and executable adversarial contracts

scope.parent_pipeline: Independent implementation and live testing are owned by the parent; this report supplies contracts, probes, and a smallest patch decision.

evidence_labels.local_evidence: Directly inspected canonical source or local offline experiment; platform observations quoted in the kit are not independently reproduced here.
evidence_labels.primary_evidence: Inspected primary paper or official documentation. Author results are not replicated Freya results.
evidence_labels.inference: Our engineering design or transfer of a research idea.
evidence_labels.unsupported: Not supported by the supplied Freya contract, or cannot be guaranteed with the seven supplied endpoints.
evidence_labels.needs_probe: Documented mechanism whose critical composition or failure semantics need a bounded parent-owned runtime test.

decision.status: RECOMMEND incremental guarded cyclic workflow; do not replace the generator with a general planner framework.
decision.summary_tr: Cümleler için dallanan ağaç yerine, küçük bir döngülü iş akışı ve bağımsız politika çekirdeği kullanın. Model anlamı, açıklamayı ve sıradaki uygun soruyu seçsin; kimlik, tarih/tutar, onay, araç yetkisi ve banka kayıtları kodla doğrulansın. Freya döngüleri destekliyor. İlk yama, mevcut PromiseRuntime semantiğini çağrı durumuna bağlayan bir olay indirgeyici ve her yazımdan önce çalışan yapısal kapı olmalı.
decision.architecture: Factored hierarchical policy state + semantic dialogue + one-step receding-horizon choice over enabled skills + capability-gated serial bank dispatch + event/result reduction.
decision.minimum_patch: Add a serializable guarded action envelope and explicit user-event/turn revision to the existing builder's generated code. Gate create_promise, add_note, transfer_to_agent and close_call through deterministic code nodes. Preserve the current generator and identity scaffolding, and reuse the existing calendar/commit semantics. Add correction_received invalidation before validating replacement terms.
decision.why_now: The re-read builder_prompts.py now explicitly calls for a compact hybrid graph and source hash integrity. It already states most desired principles, but a prompt is not an executable link to policy_runtime.py. A repository search found no importing caller for policy_runtime outside its own tests at inspection time. Make this link inspectable before adding planner/search complexity.
decision.not_claimed: No measured improvement in Freya pass rate, universal natural-language understanding, distributed exactly-once delivery, or complete unseen-brief compilation.
merge_order: Correct user-correction invalidation semantics and specify source-linked event/action schema.
Lower the result reducer and commit gate to documented code/api_request nodes; keep conversation wording free within a speech contract.
Use the eight deterministic fixtures and source mutation tests before parent-owned live deployment.
Enable deferred-note finalization only after the interruption boundary probe establishes the required ordering; otherwise expose that limitation.
release_blockers: An actual input-admission boundary for Brief B note flushing has not been established by the supplied platform docs.
An unknown write timeout cannot be reconciled using the seven supplied endpoints.
Security-answer extraction, literal readback delivery and combined correction/confirmation need transcript-level verification; structured output alone is not semantic proof.

runtime_findings.claim: Freya workflows need not be DAGs. target_node may equal the current node, and transitions back to earlier nodes are expressly supported.
runtime_findings.label: local_evidence

runtime_findings.claim: The local topology.py DAG check applies to forward specialist handoffs, excluding bounded handbacks. It is a local architecture constraint, not the Freya workflow schema.
runtime_findings.label: local_evidence

runtime_findings.claim: FlowAgent §3.1 formalizes its workflow dependency graph as a DAG. That paper's formalism must not be imported as a Freya platform restriction.
runtime_findings.label: primary_evidence

runtime_findings.claim: A finite graph does not inherently force fixed wording. The combinatorial explosion comes from encoding utterance variants, all product-state combinations and every interrupt as separate nodes.
runtime_findings.label: inference

runtime_findings.claim: Extraction -> routing -> dialogue are separate calls with separate instructions. Routing is also evaluated after tool results. Dialogue cannot directly enforce the router's interpretation.
runtime_findings.label: local_evidence

runtime_findings.claim: loop_condition runs before ordinary transitions; global interrupts run only after ordinary transitions fail. An unconditional local transition can starve a global handler, and duplicate target transitions are OR-merged.
runtime_findings.label: local_evidence

runtime_findings.claim: Seven bank endpoints exist, but their availability must differ by state. The service does not enforce brief date/floor policy and customer_id is a per-call secret, so no live IDs are included in these synthetic fixtures.
runtime_findings.label: local_evidence

runtime_findings.claim: Only HTTP envelope success AND body ok=true establish a successful action; an HTTP 200 with ok=false is not a recorded promise. A tool's transport success counter is not the business ledger.
runtime_findings.label: inference

runtime_findings.claim: The existing kernel is an in-process coordinator, not a durable log; identity, persuasion, extraction trust, transcript speech, Freya serialization and write-timeout reconciliation are adapter responsibilities.
runtime_findings.label: local_evidence

runtime_findings.claim: propose() validates before invalidating confirmation. Its test intentionally permits committing the previous terms after a rejected correction. A genuine user correction must first revoke prior assent, while an invalid planner candidate should leave assent alone.
runtime_findings.label: inference

runtime_findings.claim: begin_close() reserves closure immediately and has no close_result acknowledgement method. This enforces at-most-one local dispatch but cannot establish backend closure or recover a definite failed close.
runtime_findings.label: local_evidence

runtime_findings.claim: The IR validates source-ID coverage, names and references, not semantic completeness of the compiled policy. The independent critic is helpful but not a proof.
runtime_findings.label: local_evidence

primary_sources.title: FlowAgent: Achieving Compliance and Flexibility for Workflow Agents
primary_sources.evidence: PDL separates procedural prerequisites from dialogue. Pre-decision guidance and post-decision checking constrain model choices. Its formal dependency graph is a DAG; Freya need not be. Ordinary SGD results do not uniformly outperform the baseline.
primary_sources.inference: Borrow preconditions and postchecks, not a sentence tree or its DAG assumption.
primary_sources.limit: Manual workflow execution study; no proof of automatic unseen-brief compilation or Freya latency.

primary_sources.title: AgentSpec: Customizable Runtime Enforcement for Safe and Reliable LLM Agents
primary_sources.evidence: Runtime rules use triggers, predicates and enforcement actions. Automatically generated rules miss cases: reported embodied-agent recall is 70.96%.
primary_sources.inference: Source coverage and independent counterexamples remain necessary even with a deterministic kernel.
primary_sources.limit: A correct enforcer cannot recover omitted or semantically incorrect source rules.

primary_sources.title: Progent: Programmable Privilege Control for LLM Agents
primary_sources.evidence: Declarative policies constrain tool arguments and supply denial fallbacks. The authors explicitly exclude attacks on text output; automated policy updates trade away formal guarantees.
primary_sources.inference: Compute least privilege from trusted state; never let the dialogue model widen permissions.
primary_sources.limit: A tool gate alone cannot guarantee privacy or honesty in spoken sentences.

primary_sources.title: Vigil: Runtime Enforcement of Behavioral Specifications in AI Agent Skills
primary_sources.evidence: Typed traces and finite-trace constraints express cross-call ordering and value flow. Its trust model assumes complete event collection. Reported mean end-to-end checking cost is 4.38 seconds, mostly policy compilation.
primary_sources.inference: Use compact event monitors for whole-conversation obligations; compile off the live speech path.
primary_sources.limit: No future user intent oracle; no Freya SMT support established. We do not embed Vigil or Z3.

primary_sources.title: Robust Planning with Compound LLM Architectures: An LLM-Modulo Approach
primary_sources.evidence: A generate-test-critique loop derives soundness from sound critics; completeness depends on the generator producing relevant candidates.
primary_sources.inference: Allow bounded next-action proposals and replan after real observations, with deterministic authorization.
primary_sources.limit: Scheduling experiments are not conversational banking evidence; a larger planner does not guarantee completion.

primary_sources.title: State Chart XML (SCXML): State Machine Notation for Control Abstraction
primary_sources.evidence: Compound states, parallel regions and shallow/deep history separate state structure from event transitions.
primary_sources.inference: Represent independent identity, product and terminal dimensions as data; lower a hierarchy to Freya flat nodes.
primary_sources.limit: SCXML history/parallel semantics are not native features promised by Freya.

primary_sources.title: LangGraph Graph API overview and Persistence
primary_sources.read_scope: State/reducers, Runtime context, Recursion limit; Persistence checkpointer vs store.
primary_sources.evidence: Graph execution has a configurable step bound; state snapshots and cross-thread stores are distinct persistence mechanisms.
primary_sources.inference: Bound cyclic execution and distinguish per-call state from durable history.
primary_sources.limit: These are LangGraph features, not evidence that LangGraph imports, checkpoints or interrupts work in Freya.

primary_sources.title: Event Sourcing pattern
primary_sources.read_scope: Workflow, Pattern advantages, Issues and considerations.
primary_sources.evidence: Immutable events can be replayed to reconstruct a state projection, with separate read models.
primary_sources.inference: Keep utterance proposals, authorization and backend success as different events; latest response variables are not a ledger.
primary_sources.limit: A JSON event array in Freya vars is only per-call audit state, not a durable distributed event store.

primary_sources.title: Saga design pattern
primary_sources.read_scope: Solution; compensable, pivot and retryable transactions.
primary_sources.evidence: A saga is a sequence of local transactions with explicit compensation and a point of no return.
primary_sources.inference: Keep successful product writes; recover forward on subsequent failures.
primary_sources.limit: Freya has no compensation/cancel endpoints and A36 forbids changing recorded promises. A full rollback saga is unavailable.

primary_sources.title: tau-bench: A Benchmark for Tool-Agent-User Interaction in Real-World Domains
primary_sources.read_scope: §3 reward and pass^k; revisits existing literature S01.
primary_sources.evidence: Final database equality can miss missing confirmation. Pass^k measures repeated success across all k trials.
primary_sources.inference: Check ledger plus temporal speech/action traces and repeat the eight cases with paraphrases.
primary_sources.limit: These fixtures and local tests do not measure current Freya performance.

comparison.state_representation: One branch per utterance or path; revisits require duplication.
comparison.diversity: Poor if phrases are hard-coded; free-language nodes can still be diverse.
comparison.safety: Auditable on short paths, brittle under corrections and interruptions.
comparison.growth: Branching b over depth d can yield O(b^d) path expansion.

comparison.diversity: Not inherently restricted: a state can have an open semantic prompt.
comparison.safety: Good coarse identity gating; state explosion if all product/interrupt combinations become states.
comparison.growth: Cartesian combinations remain large if flattened; symbolic variables can avoid enumeration.
comparison.freya_fit: Directly supported by nodes, variables and transitions.
comparison.decision: Use for external-effect boundaries, not sentence choice.

comparison.state_representation: Orthogonal identity, dialogue, product and terminal state; resume focus is data.
comparison.diversity: Local dialogue freedom and reusable interrupts.
comparison.safety: Shared predicates avoid duplicated fragile edges; precedence must be explicit.
comparison.growth: Compact representation; formal exploration can still be exponential.
comparison.freya_fit: Lower to flat nodes + vars. Native nesting, deep history and parallel regions unconfirmed.
comparison.decision: Use as the policy design model.

comparison.state_representation: Enabled actions and outstanding obligations, re-evaluated after each user or tool event.
comparison.diversity: Handles novel combinations and clarifications without prewriting every path.
comparison.safety: A planner proposes; sound guards authorize. Semantic extraction remains fallible.
comparison.growth: Bound candidates and planning depth; do not run MCTS/full search per spoken turn.
comparison.freya_fit: Prompt-level action choice supported; arbitrary planner runtime/network framework unsupported.
comparison.decision: Use a one-step chooser over legal skills, not autonomous long tool sequences.

comparison.state_representation: Reusable ask/clarify/explain/verify/negotiate/readback/record/transfer/finalize skills with preconditions and results.
comparison.diversity: Wording and legal ordering can adapt; schema and authorization do not.
comparison.safety: Capabilities need state/revision/product/argument binding; seven tools is not seven permanent permissions.
comparison.growth: Approximately O(rules + skills + endpoints) graph and O(products) data for this brief; no claim that all planning is polynomial.
comparison.decision: Recommended combination with hierarchical policy state.

compiler_separation.policy_ir: Compile source clauses and explicit B-over-A replacements into typed predicates, parameters, obligations, priorities and operation schemas. Preserve provenance. LLM source extraction is a fallible front end; reject unresolved conflicts and unsupported mechanisms before export.
compiler_separation.extraction: Produce user assertions only: identity-answer text, customer/third-party status, questions, date expression, amount expression, product reference, correction/withdrawal, clear assent, and requested support/human/restructuring. Never extract trusted verified, recorded, customer_id, approved_date, closed or backend_ok from speech. Separate namespaces ex_* / st_* / dispatch_* / result_*.
compiler_separation.ambiguity: Do not collapse a mixed utterance to one intent enum: 'yes, but change the loan date' contains correction plus assent. Capture independent flags/raw spans, then prioritize corrections and policy-specific interrupts. Require an evidence turn and the current readback revision for assent. Confidence thresholds are not authorization.
compiler_separation.freshness: Reset ephemeral extraction fields to an explicit unset sentinel after consumption, with a consumed event revision. Do not interpret a still-set variable as fresh confirmation. Node current_turns resets on transitions; use an explicit call-wide count or documented total_turns, not it as a durable event ID.
compiler_separation.routing: On every new user turn route to the reducer before dialogue or an external action. The reducer computes one string route_target from validated state. Emit grouped OR comparisons, nested AND only where necessary. Do not hide mandatory interrupts behind an always edge or loop_condition.
compiler_separation.dialogue: Render a compact view: verified-safe facts, active product, remaining obligations, currently permitted speech acts, required literal lines and the next question. The model may paraphrase, answer supported questions and acknowledge emotion. It cannot announce speculative success or add financial terms.
compiler_separation.dates: Preserve raw relative-date wording even if using type=date. The default extractor anchors to system today and concretizes vague periods, while A uses supplied now and sometimes requires clarification. Override with the documented extraction placeholders plus the injected anchor, then deterministically re-resolve and validate from raw expression. Never trust extraction's guessed date as a commit date.
compiler_separation.tool_results: Normalize envelopes and true/True explicitly into string status flags; never use bool('false'). Match each result to an outstanding dispatch. Build next-action instructions from trusted status/policy, not arbitrary text in the tool payload.
compiler_separation.coverage: Map every clause to the actual extractor/routing guard/dialogue obligation/commit check/test that implements it. A source-ID row without an enforcement site is inadequate.

state_and_events.policy: policy_version and source-derived calendars, amounts, bands, retry limits, identity order, queue/outcome/reason maps; immutable for a call.
state_and_events.runtimeclock: RuntimeClock(now_iso, local_calendar_basis, source='call_variables.now') is an explicit adapter concept, not an existing class. Freeze injected now for the call. Missing/invalid now blocks date-dependent operations rather than falling back to wall time. Do not infer Europe/Istanbul from this workstation for a bank brief that supplies a naive local datetime. Physical latency uses a separate monotonic timer.
state_and_events.trusted_state: Identity stages and counters from successful normalized verification results; ordered account products from get_account; product-specific deadlines/floors; outstanding questions; refusal, hardship and vague-date counts; current readback revision; pending terminal reason; pending action; speech obligations.
state_and_events.product_state: Each product has proposed terms, confirmed terms bound to a batch revision, recorded terms and backend receipt, persuasion count, create attempt count, disposition candidate, note acknowledgement. A recorded promise is immutable; later failure on another product cannot undo it.

event_schema.kind: user_observed | extraction_candidate | correction_received | readback_emitted | confirmation_received | dispatch_reserved | backend_result | note_buffered | finalize_requested | input_closed | close_acknowledged
event_schema.action_id: optional integer from kernel, never model-selected

state_and_events.reduction: state_next = reduce(state, event, immutable_policy). Accepted user facts and actual tool receipts are distinct from proposed commands. Preserve a compact trace in vars as explicit JSON; state summaries are projections, not evidence replacing receipts. Do not store unnecessary raw security answers in summaries.
state_and_events.confirmation: Any real user correction or withdrawal invalidates the outstanding batch immediately, including an out-of-policy replacement. Validation failure must not resurrect old assent. An invalid internal planner candidate is a different event and need not revoke assent. A bare yes is valid only in direct response to the current complete readback, with no correction or overriding request in that turn.
state_and_events.partial_commit: For B, one batch readback and confirmation authorize serial create_promise calls in account order. Re-evaluate queued user events between writes. Successful products stay recorded; definitive double failures become buffered service_error; transfer discards only unrecorded proposals/confirmations and buffered notes.
state_and_events.state_size: Per-product records and an active index replace product-specific graph copies. The representational improvement is linear in product count for these fields; reachable combinations and verification remain potentially exponential.

capability_gates.allow: Confirmed customer on the line; expected security field only; refusal/attempt budget permits another answer; normalized answer present.
capability_gates.deny: Relative offering answers; later-field bypass; exhausted check. A swapped-date hint does not consume a wrong answer.

capability_gates.allow: Both required checks succeeded according to actual verification responses for this customer.
capability_gates.deny: A user's 'I passed' or assistant inference cannot enable it.

capability_gates.allow: Identity verified; known product; current explicit batch confirmation; exact terms valid under RuntimeClock and product policy; unrecorded; no transfer requested; retry budget; next ordered product; no in-flight call.
capability_gates.deny: Stale assent, hypothetical offer, fabricated product, under-floor amount, wrong clock/date, or already recorded.

capability_gates.allow: B enables notes; product has no recorded promise; disposition reason valid; actual non-transfer input boundary established; final flush in account order; not previously acknowledged.
capability_gates.deny: A always; any transfer anywhere in this call; early eager notes; unclassified products.

capability_gates.allow: Third-party callback path; today or next business day; time in [10:00,19:00]; strictly later than injected now; at most one alternative request after an invalid offer.
capability_gates.deny: Using a holiday as next business day or a past time; third-party security/account actions remain unavailable.

capability_gates.allow: Source-defined human/restructuring/support trigger with required prior ask/acceptance; queue from supplied schema; no in-flight effect; no note has been written in B.
capability_gates.deny: Invented queue, automatic transfer to solve unknown data, or transferring after notes merely because the model asks.

capability_gates.allow: All applicable obligations resolved, goodbye emitted, no in-flight action, required notes acknowledged on non-transfer path or transfer acknowledged, correct deterministic reduction; no earlier dispatch of close.
capability_gates.deny: Claimed success without receipt; unresolved products on non-transfer B path; any later bank action.

design.close_reducer: For identified/account-loaded B calls: successful transfer wins; else any recorded promise wins after all required dispositions/notes; else all paid -> paid; else first non-paid disposition in get_account order -> no_promise/reason. Pre-identity branches use A's own not_reached/not_verified/transfer rules and do not invent products or notes. A suppresses notes entirely.

planning_and_adaptation.allowed: The dialogue can choose how to clarify, which supported question to answer, whether a user utterance changes the pending task, and which enabled skill serves the next obligation. Choose one next action, execute at most one effect, then recompute from the observation. Strict product order and persuasion rules still constrain choice.
planning_and_adaptation.forbidden: The live model cannot add tools, edit policy predicates or constants, reinterpret its own tool success, rewrite ledger history, train weights, run arbitrary Python, or authorize itself.
planning_and_adaptation.skill_contract: Each reusable skill carries id, preconditions, read/write set, allowed speech facts, required speech, postconditions, interruption rule, budget and source IDs. Skills are internal compiled operations, not newly exposed bank endpoints.
planning_and_adaptation.model_selection: README fixes the phone-agent model to AGENT_LLM. Builder models may differ; the researcher request does not authorize changing deployed phone models. Simulation overrides must match the event rules. reasoning_override exists but only works for supporting models; it is not a verified adaptive-model facility.
planning_and_adaptation.adaptation_scope: Adapt prompts, semantic focus and action proposals inside the fixed kernel. At build time an independent critic may propose a bounded repair from source-linked counterexamples, followed by held-out and mutation checks. No live learning or permission expansion from customer text.
planning_and_adaptation.latency: Do not add multi-agent debate, MCTS, SMT compilation or repeated critic models to each voice turn. Reuse Freya's existing extraction/routing/dialogue path and small code reducers. Bound planner retries and global tool/turn loops; preserve source counts and flag a noncompliant timeout outcome instead of inventing one.
planning_and_adaptation.unknown_scenarios: A new phrasing or combination can map to existing facts and skills. A genuinely absent bank operation is unavailable; A44 requires an honest information limit. Novelty does not grant authority.

freya_lowering.baseline: Use ordinary cyclic nodes; no new server, framework import, custom handler or endpoint. Keep bank APIs out of free-dialogue tool arrays in the smallest strict variant. Capabilities are code-authorized reachability to seven fixed dispatch nodes, not 2^7 copies of tool subsets.

logical_nodes.name: init_state
logical_nodes.purpose: Initialize every state/sentinel, policy version, injected clock, counters and route target. Verify mandatory call variables without printing customer_id.

logical_nodes.name: opening / identity_dialogue
logical_nodes.purpose: Required first disclosure and who-is-speaking question; collect only user assertions. No account tools. Every user event goes through reduce_user.

logical_nodes.name: security_dialogue
logical_nodes.purpose: One current security question and corrections/questions; sensitive data unavailable. Routing depends on reduce_user and actual verify results.

logical_nodes.name: service_dialogue
logical_nodes.purpose: All-products disclosure once, negotiation, questions, hardship and selected safe skills. One reusable node, active product stored in data. No arbitrary external calls.

logical_nodes.name: readback
logical_nodes.purpose: Render the exact ordered batch product/amount/date facts, ask for confirmation and wait for a user turn. Entering the node alone is not proof a complete line was delivered.

logical_nodes.name: reduce_user
logical_nodes.purpose: Consume fresh extraction fields; process questions plus corrections plus interrupts; invalidate assent when needed; calculate allowed action/arguments and dialogue view; route once.

logical_nodes.name: dispatch_verify / dispatch_account / dispatch_promise / dispatch_callback / dispatch_transfer / dispatch_note
logical_nodes.purpose: One fixed endpoint per bank operation, fully baked args from guarded dispatch_* variables. No model-supplied customer_id/product/status fields. maxRetries=0 for writes; preferably connect_retries=0 for deterministic attempt accounting.

logical_nodes.name: reduce_result
logical_nodes.purpose: Normalize the actual response, consume one matching pending action, keep per-product partial commits, refresh all dispatch fields and speech obligations before returning to dialogue or the next warranted action.

logical_nodes.name: goodbye / finalize_gate
logical_nodes.purpose: Say goodbye before close. Finalize only when the last admitted user event is reduced. Freeze terminal branch and flush B notes only if the real input boundary probe passes.

logical_nodes.name: dispatch_close -> end
logical_nodes.purpose: Dispatch close_call once with reduced outcome/reason; route on normalized result to platform hangup without another bank call. Post-hook may record acknowledgement; no bank effect after close.

freya_lowering.scheduling: conversation receives user -> extraction -> always transition to reduce_user -> deterministic route -> conversation on_enter speaks and waits, OR guarded API node runs -> reduce_result -> next conversation/action. Never make the dialogue node passthrough during ordinary conversation. Avoid unconditional passthrough cycles. User and tool events must have distinct consumption markers so reduce_result cannot accidentally reconfirm a previous yes.
freya_lowering.state_transport: Serialize JSON-safe state and events explicitly through vars; object identity of Python BackendAttempt cannot survive separate sandbox invocations. Replace identity checks in the emitter with a kernel-owned action_id, expected operation, bound arguments, policy/state revision and dispatch status. This is logical integrity within trusted code, not a cryptographic token.
freya_lowering.baking: All required dispatch fields are set before entering api_request, ensuring default binding sees validated values. Do not rely on changing vars after tool registration to refresh baked arguments. A stale default can silently replace a new model value. Clear previous result/status fields before dispatch; never reuse a success from the previous product.
freya_lowering.sandbox: Only json/re/datetime imports are verified. Do not import policy_runtime.py, dataclasses, Decimal, Z3 or LangGraph into Freya by assumption. Generate small equivalent JSON-state code using verified modules; differential-test against the local Python oracle. Avoid adjacent double braces anywhere in snippets; initialize safe fallback values and catch exceptions to deny dispatch.
freya_lowering.money: Local oracle uses Decimal; target emission can compare canonical decimal strings or scaled integers losslessly. Decimal import is unconfirmed. Neither the brief nor OpenAPI supplies a cent quantum: do not silently add quantum=0.01 as policy. Bind a quantum only when a source states one; otherwise preserve exact admissible decimals and reject malformed/nonfinite values. Test wire numeric serialization separately.
freya_lowering.result_instruction: Return trusted next-action facts via rendered dialogue view or a code-authored post-hook message. Strip irrelevant headers. An API payload's arbitrary 'what_to_do_next' text must not become authority.
freya_lowering.turn_budget: Track total conversation user events and non-speaking internal steps explicitly. Freya current_turns resets on reentry; max_node_turns without max_turn_transition does not terminate. Budgets prevent accidental loops but cannot invent a source-approved closing reason.
freya_lowering.deployment_validation: Parent must save/export/read back the workflow and compare retained fields, then run the official fixed models. This task does not call Freya.

unsupported_features.feature: Native SCXML hierarchy, parallel regions, history stack
unsupported_features.replacement: Flatten macro states; retain active_product and resume_focus explicitly.

unsupported_features.feature: Dynamic per-turn replacement of tool schemas/capabilities
unsupported_features.replacement: Static dispatch nodes plus deterministic guard edges; no direct bank tools in unrestricted dialogue.

unsupported_features.feature: A pre-hook exception reliably cancels an HTTP request
unsupported_features.replacement: Deny by routing before API-node entry. Do not use raise, bad URL or empty body as the security barrier.

unsupported_features.feature: code_exec model tool top-level args and execution semantics
unsupported_features.status: documented but not verified by kit

unsupported_features.replacement: Use bounded explicit {{variable}} projections in prompt strings.
Generate self-contained json/re/datetime code and supplied API calls only.

unsupported_features.feature: Guaranteed atomic note-flush plus close and barge-in admission cutoff
unsupported_features.replacement: Probe an actual noninteractive finalization boundary; otherwise report B10 race unsolved.

unsupported_features.feature: Idempotency key, transaction, rollback, promise cancellation or query-by-operation receipt
unsupported_features.replacement: Serial writes, preserve acknowledged partial commits, no blind retry after unknown outcome.
At-most-once local dispatch plus explicit pending/acknowledged/unknown state; detect crash/recovery gaps.

unsupported_features.feature: Dynamic phone model swaps, weight updates or external planner calls
unsupported_features.status: model fixed / only bank API permitted by event rules
unsupported_features.replacement: Adapt language/focus within fixed model; change builder models only.

unsupported_features.feature: Blocking or rewriting arbitrary streamed speech before it reaches caller
unsupported_features.replacement: Minimize pre-verification facts; use deterministic mandated phrases where needed and transcript-level tests. Free-text privacy/honesty remain semantic residual risks.

whole_conversation_and_failure_semantics.note_barrier: B10 is a whole-trace property: transfer_exists => no add_note anywhere. Buffer dispositions, do not call add_note while the conversation can still select transfer. An internal finalize_non_transfer lock only prevents transfer execution; it does not prove compliance if the caller can still insist on a human. A valid barrier requires that all previously admitted user events are processed and no new policy-relevant input can be admitted before notes/close complete.
whole_conversation_and_failure_semantics.impossibility: For any open prefix ending just after an irreversible note, an allowed future user continuation can demand transfer. With no undo endpoint, an online controller cannot both honor that continuation and erase the prior note. This is an architectural inference, not a Freya observed failure. Either an actual input cutoff makes the conversation finite, or the platform/brief must resolve the conflict. A longer FSM or a smarter model cannot remove it.
whole_conversation_and_failure_semantics.concrete_terminal_sequence: Drain admitted user events -> resolve transfer priority -> emit required final speech/goodbye -> establish real input closure -> freeze terminal choice -> B non-transfer: add_note acknowledgements in order -> close_call once -> end_call. If the platform admits a user turn before closure, abort tentative finalization and re-reduce it; nothing irreversible should have been flushed yet.
whole_conversation_and_failure_semantics.lifecycle_caution: end_of_call tools run after call analysis and before judging; response_mapping is not applied then. The docs do not establish ordered multi-call transactional flushing. Do not substitute an end-of-call LLM summary for explicit bank outcome state.
whole_conversation_and_failure_semantics.attempts: Use policy attempts per product, not total transport-success counters. A create_promise HTTP 500 is explicitly definite no-write in this mock, so A37 allows one repeat. An HTTP 200 ok=false likewise means no action was carried out. Timeout/disconnect after dispatch is unknown, not definite failure.
whole_conversation_and_failure_semantics.unknown_result: Keep the outstanding attempt pending, prevent a second write, and retain a pending user interrupt. A late response matching that attempt may settle it, then the interrupt wins before further writes. With no late response or reconciliation endpoint, the call is observably incomplete; never fabricate service_error, recorded or transferred as success.
whole_conversation_and_failure_semantics.partial_commits: Success on p1 followed by two definite failures on p2 retains p1, marks p2 service_error, continues eligible p3, and records only missing-product notes at a valid non-transfer boundary. Transfer after p1 preserves p1 and abandons every unrecorded promise and note candidate.
whole_conversation_and_failure_semantics.close_error: Current begin_close reserves a terminal send, not a receipt. Track close_dispatched/close_acknowledged/close_unknown explicitly. A46's exactly-one close call and OpenAPI's repeatable-500 description have an unresolved edge if close itself fails: do not silently use generic automatic retries and claim both requirements. A successful complete fixture has exactly one close dispatch; failure is a failed evaluation, not a fabricated alternate outcome.
whole_conversation_and_failure_semantics.priority: Contextual source priority beats generic route priority: hardship handling precedes persuasion/restructuring when applicable, proposed date/amount is not refusal, and an actual transfer dominates a previous promise at close. An open question and a correction can coexist in one user turn.

invariant_examples: create_dispatched(p,terms,r) implies identity_verified AND known_product(p) AND confirmed_batch_revision=r AND unchanged_since_readback AND valid_terms(p,terms,RuntimeClock) AND not_recorded(p) AND no_pending_transfer AND no_inflight_action.
Any correction_received invalidates outstanding confirmation BEFORE replacement validation; no fresh clear yes means no create.
recorded(p) grows only from matching create_promise receipt with HTTP success and body ok=true; never from customer or assistant text.
A transfer result cannot erase recorded(p), but it clears every unrecorded proposal and every buffered note.
If any transfer is dispatched, the complete bank trace contains zero add_note calls.
Every complete trace has one final close_call and the goodbye precedes its dispatch.
A denial has zero bank-call side effects and returns a legal next dialogue step.

# Read-only local probe of the current repository kernel; no API I/O.
import json
import sys
from datetime import date, datetime
from pathlib import Path
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path.cwd() / "skill-creator-skill-lift"))
from agent_forge.policy_runtime import CalendarPolicy, MoneyPolicy, ProductPolicy, PromiseRuntime, CloseRules, CloseDecision, PolicyViolation
source = {"source_ids":["L03:A17-A38","L04:B10"],"purpose":"analysis-only synthetic probe"}
cal = CalendarPolicy(datetime.fromisoformat("2026-10-23T18:50"),frozenset(date.fromisoformat(x) for x in
    ["2026-10-26","2026-11-11","2026-11-26","2026-12-25","2027-01-01"]),frozenset(range(5)),0,source)
# The quantum is a fixture precision, not an asserted policy from the official brief.
p = ProductPolicy("synthetic-product",MoneyPolicy("300","1200","0.01",source),date(2026,11,12),2,source)
def fresh():
    return PromiseRuntime([p],calendar=cal,emit_product_notes=True,source_policy_parameters=source)
rules = CloseRules(CloseDecision("promise"),CloseDecision("paid"),"paid",
    {x:CloseDecision("no_promise",x) for x in ["refused","hardship","dispute","service_error"]},
    {x:CloseDecision("transferred",x) for x in ["human","support","restructuring"]},
    "outcome","reason",source)
r = fresh()
r.propose(p.product_id,"500","2026-10-30")
r.confirm(r.readback(),accepted=True)
try:
    r.propose(p.product_id,"1","2026-10-30")
except PolicyViolation as exc:
    rejected = [v.code for v in exc.violations]
confirmation_survives = r.state(p.product_id).confirmed is not None
try:
    attempt = r.begin_record(p.product_id)
    old_commit_permitted = True
except PolicyViolation:
    old_commit_permitted = False
r2 = fresh()
r2.set_note(p.product_id,"paid")
r2.finalize_non_transfer(rules)
try:
    r2.begin_transfer("human",rules=rules)
    late_transfer = "accepted"
except PolicyViolation as exc:
    late_transfer = [v.code for v in exc.violations]
assert cal.add_business_days(cal.today,7).isoformat() == "2026-11-04"
assert cal.add_business_days(cal.today,12).isoformat() == "2026-11-12"
assert cal.weekday_date(0,"next",next_weekday_semantics="following_calendar_week").isoformat() == "2026-10-26"
assert cal.next_business_day("2026-10-26",inclusive=True).isoformat() == "2026-10-27"
print(json.dumps({"invalid_replacement_errors":rejected,
 "confirmation_survives_invalid_propose":confirmation_survives,
 "old_commit_permitted_after_invalid_propose":old_commit_permitted,
 "late_transfer_after_internal_finalize":late_transfer,
 "has_close_result_method":hasattr(r2,"close_result"),
 "late_deadline":"2026-11-04","early_deadline":"2026-11-12",
 "interpretation":"Observed local API behavior; a user-correction adapter must revoke assent first. No bank write was made."},indent=2))

failure_modes.mitigation: Explicit sentinels, consumption IDs, clear result fields and unknown fallback.

failure_modes.mitigation: Trusted verification stages plus reachable dispatch gates; pre-identity safe dialogue facts.

failure_modes.mitigation: Revoke assent before validating a user-requested replacement.
